key_insight: Coherent noise can drive the surface code into a partially decodable critical phase, dual to algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking in a quantum paramagnet.
engineering_relevance: The results show that coherent errors can produce recovery regimes beyond a simple correctable–uncorrectable divide, motivating noise-aware decoder evaluation.
method: Study single-qubit Pauli-Z rotations followed by syndrome measurements on a triangular-lattice surface code.
Relate decoding to strongly symmetric decoherence in a Z₂ paramagnet through Wegner duality.
Derive universal signatures using an SO(n) nonlinear sigma model in the replica limit n→1.
evidence_signal: Large-scale numerical simulations confirm analytical predictions for aspect-ratio-dependent optimal Pauli decoding fidelity and power-law decay of a dual fidelity correlator.
watch_item: The predictions concern an idealized coherent-noise model and thermodynamic-limit behavior; performance under realistic mixed hardware noise remains to be established.
paper_title: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code
